mainTopic: טומאה during צרעת and hair-growth days, רב חסדא's 'no fix' after the blood, and which איסורים still apply to a נזיר whose days are complete.
overview: The amud opens with a second argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. A נזיר who had צרעת became טמא מת during his צרעת. Does that wipe out (סותר) his earlier days? רבי יוחנן says yes, because he is still inside his נזירות. ריש לקיש says no, because צרעת and נזירות are separate. The גמרא explains why this argument must be recorded both here and in the earlier case of נזירות for a son. Next, רב and שמואל argue about טומאה during the hair-growth days after the צרעת, and each shows his view fits even the opposing אמורא. רב חסדא then rules that once the hair was made holy by the blood, טומאה leaves 'no fix'. The גמרא explains he follows the רבנן and means only the מצוה of shaving. Finally, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא rules that a נזיר whose days are over still gets מלקות for טומאה, but not for shaving or wine. The גמרא challenges why the word 'כל' does not extend shaving and wine too, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Impurity during the days of leprosy: does it wipe out the earlier days?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says טומאה during the days of צרעת is סותר the earlier נזירות days; ריש לקיש says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a נזיר became impure during the days of his צרעת: רבי יוחנן says it cancels his earlier days. ריש לקיש says it does not cancel them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a נזיר who is a מצורע and becomes טמא מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally טומאת מת during נזירות is סותר, meaning the נזיר must start counting again. Here the problem is that during צרעת the days do not count toward נזירות, but they also do not cancel it. So it is unclear whether the נזיר is still 'in' his נזירות and can lose his earlier days.

keyTerms.meaning: became impure (here, through contact with a dead body)
the skin disease of the Torah, often called leprosy
cancels the days already counted, so he must start over
does not cancel the earlier days

steps.confusionAlert: The days of צרעת themselves are not counted toward the נזירות no matter what. The argument is only about whether the טומאה cancels the days he counted BEFORE he got צרעת.

phrases.english: If he became impure during the days of his leprosy —
phrases.notes: Picture a נזיר who got צרעת in the middle of his נזירות, and then also became טמא מת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: it negates.
phrases.notes: It wipes out the נזירות days he counted before the צרעת.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: it does not negate.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: סוֹתֵר. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵינוֹ סוֹתֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second case with the same מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש as the earlier case on the daf (טומאה during the נזירות taken on for a son).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: טומאה during the days of צרעת is סותר the earlier נזירות days. ריש לקיש: it is not סותר.

steps.title: The reasons behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds the מצורע is still in his נזירות. ריש לקיש holds צרעת and נזירות are two separate things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it cancels, because he is still standing in his נזירות. ריש לקיש says it does not cancel, because צרעת is one thing and נזירות is another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, צרעת only pauses the counting, but the person is still a נזיר, so טומאה hits his נזירות like any other טומאה. For ריש לקיש, the time of צרעת is its own separate period and is not part of the נזירות at all, so a טומאה during that time does not touch the נזירות days.

keyTerms.meaning: he is still standing in (inside) his נזירות

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the מצורע is still inside his נזירות, so it is סותר. ריש לקיש: צרעת לחוד ונזירות לחוד, so it is not סותר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says it negates,
since he is still standing in naziriteship.
Reish Lakish says it does not negate —
leprosy is separate and naziriteship is separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the two rulings stated in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן's reason: the מצורע is still inside his נזירות. ריש לקיש's reason: צרעת and נזירות are separate periods.

steps.title: Why the argument is needed in this case too
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the first case (נזירות for a son), we might think רבי יוחנן would agree with ריש לקיש in the צרעת case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both cases are needed. If the argument were taught only in the first case, I would say that רבי יוחנן said it cancels there because it is all one name of נזירות. But here I would say he agrees with ריש לקיש, since being a נזיר is separate and צרעת is separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it does not say out loud: why record the same argument twice? It begins by showing why the צרעת case is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the son case, both periods are real נזירות, so it is easy to say the טומאה hits everything. In the צרעת case, the צרעת time is not נזירות at all. So without this case we could have thought even רבי יוחנן admits the טומאה is not סותר there.

keyTerms.meaning: it is necessary (to teach both cases)
the first one, the earlier case
one single name or label of נזירות

phrases.english: And it is necessary, for if it were stated only in that first case,
phrases.notes: The first case is the earlier one on this daf: a נזיר who became impure during the נזירות he took on for his son's birth.

phrases.english: in that case Rabbi Yochanan said it negates —
because it is one name of naziriteship.
But in this case, I would say
he agrees with Reish Lakish,
since being a nazir is separate and leprosy is separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the dispute itself to the question of why it is recorded both here and in the earlier son case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something the other could not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the son case alone, we might think רבי יוחנן agrees that טומאה during צרעת is not סותר, because צרעת is not נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The צרעת case teaches that רבי יוחנן holds it is סותר even here.

steps.title: Why the argument is needed in the first case too, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the צרעת case, we might think ריש לקיש would agree with רבי יוחנן in the son case. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the argument were taught only in this case, I would say ריש לקיש said it does not cancel only here. But in that first case I would say he agrees with רבי יוחנן. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא by showing the other direction. The son case is also needed, so both cases must be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's reason here, that צרעת is not נזירות, does not apply in the son case, where both periods are נזירות. So from the צרעת case alone we might think ריש לקיש agrees it is סותר in the son case. Recording both cases shows that each אמורא holds his view in both situations.

keyTerms.meaning: I would say (we might have thought)

steps.whatToRemember: Each case alone could mislead: the son case might suggest רבי יוחנן gives in on צרעת, and the צרעת case might suggest ריש לקיש gives in on the son case. So the גמרא needs both, and each side keeps his view in both.

phrases.english: And if it were stated only in this case,
in this case Reish Lakish said [it does not negate],
but in that case —
I would say he agrees with Rabbi Yochanan,
[therefore] it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכותא that began in step 3 and closes with 'צריכא'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases must be taught, because each one shows that its אמורא keeps his view where we might have thought he would agree with the other.

steps.title: רב: becoming impure during the hair-growth days does not cancel the earlier days
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that טומאה during the days of גידול שער does not cancel the earlier days. He says this holds even for רבי יוחנן, because those days come after the נזירות and are not inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the נזיר became impure during the days his hair was growing back, רב says this does not cancel his earlier days. Even רבי יוחנן, who said impurity does cancel, would agree here. רבי יוחנן only meant a case where the person is still in the middle of his נזירות. The hair-growth days are an addition after the נזירות, not part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case built on the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and gives רב's ruling: the earlier days are not cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said טומאה is סותר because the מצורע is still inside his נזירות. רב says the hair-growth days are different, because they come after the נזירות is already finished. So even רבי יוחנן's reason does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Hair growth. These are the days a cured מצורע waits for his hair to grow back so he can do the נזיר shaving.
It does not cancel (the earlier days).
An addition after the נזירות, not part of the נזירות itself.

phrases.english: If he became impure on the days of hair growth.
phrases.notes: This is a נזיר who had צרעת, was cured and shaved, and is now waiting for his hair to grow back.

phrases.english: Rav said: it does not cancel (the earlier days).
Even according to Rabbi Yochanan, who says it cancels,
that applies only where he is still in his נזירות;
but the hair-growth time is an addition after the נזירות.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְמָא בְּיוֹם גִּידּוּל שֵׂעָר. רַב אָמַר: אֵינוֹ סוֹתֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argument to look at a new case: the hair-growth days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impurity during the hair-growth days does not cancel, even according to רבי יוחנן, because those days are an addition after the נזירות.

steps.title: שמואל: becoming impure during the hair-growth days does cancel the earlier days
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees and says it is סותר. He says this holds even for ריש לקיש, because here there is only one נזירות, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: it does cancel. Even ריש לקיש, who said impurity does not cancel, would agree here. ריש לקיש was talking about a case with two separate נזירות. Here there is only one נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposite ruling from רב, and shows it works even according to ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said אינו סותר in the earlier case of the נזירות for a son, where there were two separate נזירות periods, so impurity in one did not harm the other. שמואל says the hair-growth days complete this one נזירות. So impurity during those days damages the נזירות itself.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל each show that his view fits even the side he seems to oppose. רב says the hair-growth days are outside the נזירות, so there is no cancelling. שמואל says they are part of one נזירות, so there is cancelling.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: it cancels.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמַר אֵין סוֹתֵר —
phrases.english: Even according to Reish Lakish, who says it does not cancel,
there it is two separate נזירות periods,
phrases.notes: He means the earlier case of the נזירות for a son, where there were two real נזירות: his own and the one for his son.

phrases.english: here it is one נזירות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to רב's ruling in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impurity during the hair-growth days cancels, even according to ריש לקיש, because here it is one נזירות.

steps.title: רב חסדא: if the hair was made holy by the blood, there is no fix
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says everyone agrees that if the hair was already made holy through the sprinkling of the blood, and the נזיר then became impure, he has no fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Everyone agrees that if the hair was made holy through the blood, he has no fix.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רב חסדא gives a rule that he says everyone agrees to, about a נזיר who became impure after his final offerings were brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the blood of the נזיר's final offering is sprinkled, his hair is holy and waiting to be shaved. If he becomes impure at that point, רב חסדא says nothing can fix it. The גמרא will next ask what 'no fix' means.

keyTerms.meaning: The hair became holy through the sprinkling of the blood of the offering.
He has no fix or remedy.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁאִם קִדֵּשׁ שֵׂעָר בַּדָּם —
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that if the hair was made holy through the blood,
phrases.notes: The case is that he became impure after the blood was sprinkled but before he shaved.

phrases.english: he has no fix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a statement that everyone agrees to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impurity after the hair was made holy by the blood leaves the נזיר with no fix.

steps.title: Whose opinion does רב חסדא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא רב חסדא's rule matches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking whose view רב חסדא is following. It will now test each possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument about whether shaving is required to finish the נזירות. The גמרא wants to see which side of that argument רב חסדא's rule fits.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source of רב חסדא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion רב חסדא's rule follows.

steps.title: It cannot follow רבי אליעזר, since then the impurity should just cancel
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אליעזר, shaving is required to finish the נזירות. So the נזיר is still inside his term, and the impurity should simply cancel his days. He would not be left with 'no fix.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי אליעזר: since he says shaving is required, the impurity happened within the full term. So let it cancel the days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, רבי אליעזר, and shows it does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the נזירות is not over until he shaves. So impurity before shaving is like impurity in the middle of the term. The normal result is that the days are cancelled and he starts again, which is a fix, not 'no fix.'

keyTerms.meaning: The shaving is required. Without it the נזירות is not finished.
Within the full term (of the נזירות).

phrases.english: If according to Rabbi Eliezer,
since he says the shaving is required,
it is within the full term, so let it cancel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רב חסדא's rule as following רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי אליעזר the impurity happens inside the נזירות, so the days should simply be cancelled. That is a fix, which goes against 'no fix.'

steps.title: It cannot follow the רבנן either, since for them the נזירות is already over
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold shaving is not required. So after the blood is sprinkled the נזירות is finished, and impurity should not cause any problem at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows the רבנן? But they say shaving is not required!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option, the רבנן, and raises a problem with that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, once the blood is sprinkled he is no longer a נזיר, even without shaving. So becoming impure afterward should not matter. Then why would he need any fix?

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view that argues with רבי אליעזר.
The shaving is not required to finish the נזירות.

phrases.english: Rather, according to the Rabbis?
But they say the shaving is not required!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible answer after the first one failed.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רב חסדא's rule as following the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the רבנן the נזירות is already over, so impurity causes no problem and there is nothing that needs fixing.

steps.title: It follows the רבנן: 'no fix' means no way to do the מצוה of shaving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא really follows the רבנן. 'No fix' only means he cannot do the מצוה of shaving properly anymore.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it follows the רבנן. What does 'he has no fix' mean? He has no fix for the מצוה of shaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רב חסדא follows the רבנן, and it explains his words in a narrower way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His נזירות is finished, so nothing is cancelled. But the מצוה of shaving after the offerings can no longer be done the right way, and that is what he cannot fix. The problem from step 10 goes away because 'no fix' is about the shaving, not about the נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in fact. This word introduces the answer the גמרא ends up with.
The מצוה of shaving at the end of the נזירות.

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא follows the רבנן, who say shaving is not required. His 'no fix' does not mean the נזירות is ruined. It means the נזיר lost the chance to do the מצוה of shaving properly.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'אין לו תקנה' as meaning his whole נזירות is ruined. The גמרא limits it to the מצוה of shaving alone.

phrases.english: Really, it is according to the Rabbis,
and what does 'he has no fix' mean?
He has no fix for the מצוה of shaving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 10 by explaining what 'no fix' means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the words in a narrower way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No fix' seemed to mean the נזירות itself could not be repaired, which does not fit the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No fix' means only that the מצוה of shaving can no longer be done properly, which fits the רבנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא follows the רבנן. Impurity after the blood was sprinkled takes away the מצוה of shaving, not the נזירות.

steps.title: A finished נזיר is flogged for impurity but not for shaving or wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא rules that a נזיר whose days are complete gets מלקות for טומאה, but not for shaving or wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא said: A נזיר whose days are finished is flogged for becoming impure, but he is not flogged for shaving or for drinking wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new topic. It is about a נזיר who has finished his days but has not yet finished the process with his קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though his count is over, one איסור still fully applies to him: טומאה. The other two איסורים, shaving and wine, no longer carry מלקות at this stage. This uneven rule is what the next steps will question.

keyTerms.meaning: impurity, here from a dead body

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
A nazir whose days are completed
phrases.notes: He has finished counting his days but has not yet brought his קרבנות.

phrases.english: is flogged for impurity,
but he is not flogged for shaving
nor for wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about a נזיר after his days are finished. It is not tied to the רב חסדא discussion in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After his days are complete, a נזיר gets מלקות for טומאה but not for shaving or wine.

steps.title: Why is impurity different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes טומאה different, so that he is still flogged for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about impurity, that he is flogged for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule. It is setting up the source that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three איסורים normally belong to the נזירות period. So why should only טומאה continue after the days are over? The גמרא wants a source for this difference.

phrases.english: What is different about impurity, that he is flogged?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and reason why טומאה brings מלקות even after the נזיר's days are complete.

steps.title: The word 'all' includes the days after completion
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'כל ימי הזירו', and the word 'כל' includes the days after the term ends, just like the days before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verse says, 'All the days that he has set himself apart to ה׳.' This comes to include the days after completion, treating them like the days before completion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The source is the extra word 'כל' (all) in the פסוק about טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All the days' is read as including more than the counted days. It also covers the time after the count, until he brings his קרבנות. So the איסור of טומאה, with its מלקות, still applies then.

phrases.english: Because the verse says:
"All the days that he has set himself apart to ה׳"
to include the days after completion
like the days before completion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'כל' in 'כל ימי הזירו' extends the טומאה איסור to the days after completion.

steps.title: Shaving should also bring lashes
steps.stepSummary: If 'כל' extends the איסור, then the פסוק about shaving also says 'כל', so he should be flogged for shaving too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should also be liable for shaving. After all, the Torah says, 'All the days of his nazir vow, a razor shall not pass over his head.' That should make the days after completion like the days before completion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The same word 'כל' appears in the פסוק about shaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'כל' teaches that the days after completion count, it should work the same way for shaving. Then רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule that there is no מלקות for shaving would be wrong.

phrases.english: If so,
he should also be liable for shaving,
since the Merciful One said
"All the days of his nazir vow
a razor shall not pass over his head",
to make the days after completion
like the days before completion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of step 14 against the part of step 12 about shaving.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 12 that a finished נזיר is not flogged for shaving.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The shaving פסוק also has 'כל'. If 'כל' includes the days after completion for טומאה, it should do the same for shaving.

steps.title: Wine should also bring lashes
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about wine also says 'כל', so he should be flogged for wine after completion too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further, the Torah says, 'All the days of his נזירות, from anything made from the grapevine.' That should make the days after completion like the days before completion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge of the same kind, this time about wine. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine פסוק also opens with 'כל'. Now all three איסורים have the same word, so the גמרא needs to explain why only טומאה extends past completion.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the rule is wrong yet. It is showing that 'כל' alone cannot explain why only טומאה is different. An answer is still needed.

phrases.english: And furthermore,
"All the days of his nezirus
from anything that is made from the grapevine",
to make the days after completion
like the days before completion?
